blocks.text: An application is a fully qualified domain name (FQDN), local domain name, or IP address that you define on a standard set of ports. Applications must be defined within an application segment.
To enable application discovery, you can define an application as an FQDN in wildcard format or as an IP subnet.

An application segment is a grouping of defined applications, based upon access type or user privileges. Features such as double encryption, health reporting, etc. are configured per application segment.
Defining your applications in application segments enables you to:

blocks.item: Restrict access to excess ports for the application, reducing the application's attack surface.
Leverage the application segments in access policies to restrict user groups that can access them, as well as reduce lateral movement.
Apply advanced capabilities that you are licensed for such as Browser Access, Zero Trust Browser, AppProtection, and data loss prevention.

blocks.heading: About the Defined Application Segments Page

blocks.text: On the Defined Application Segments page (Private Access > Private Applications > Defined Application Segments), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Add an application segment.
Select the Show Recommendation Before Editing option.
Open the Column Menu to:
Validate a client hostname.
If you are using a Microtenant, this option is hidden.
Expand all rows in the table to see more information about each application segment. Alternatively, you can click on the Expand icon next to the name of an application segment to see its information.
Set application segment configuration warnings.
Download the configuration information for the application segments to a CSV file. The file lists the application segments based on the selected table filters.
View and add DNS search domains.
DNS search domains are unique per customer. When configuring Microtenants, DNS search domains that are added in the default tenant are inherited across Microtenants.
Configure a private link domain.
Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied.

If you are using a Microtenant, then the Microtenant Ownership Type filter is available. By default, the Configured within Microtenant filter option is applied to show the application segments configured within that specific Microtenant. The options for the filter are based on access type (Global, Configured within Microtenant, Shared to this Microtenant, and Shared from this Microtenant). If you are within the Default Microtenant, the Configured within Microtenant and Shared to this Microtenant filter options are supported. The only available operator for this filter type is Equals. By default, the Federated By filter option is set to My Tenant and applied to the application segments that are federated by your tenant. The options for the filter are My Tenant or Partner. The only available operator for this filter type is Equals.
View a list of all application segments that were configured for your organization. For each application segment, you can see:
Name: The name of the application segment.
Click the Expand icon next to an application segment to view its information.
Description: The description for the application segment.
Segment Group: The segment group that the application segment is a member of.
Double Encryption: Indicates whether Double Encryption is enabled or disabled for all applications. By default, if a Browser Access-enabled application was defined, Double Encryption is disabled.
Source IP Anchor: Indicates if Source IP Anchoring, for use with Internet & SaaS (ZIA), is enabled or disabled for all applications.
Disaster Recovery: Indicates if Disaster Recovery is enabled or disabled for the application segment.
Bypass during Reauthentication: Indicates whether Bypass during Reauthentication is enabled or disabled for the application segment.
DNS Check for FQDN domains: Indicates if any FQDN domains are associated with the application segment.
Server Group Type: The server group the application segment is a member of.
Tags: The tags associated with the application segment.
Server Groups: The server groups that the applications are hosted on.
Bypass: Indicates whether users can bypass Private Access to access applications.
ICMP Access: Indicates if ICMP communication is enabled or disabled for all applications.
Multimatch: Indicates if Multimatch is enabled or disabled for the application segment.
Load Balancing Server Groups: Indicates whether Load Balancing Server Groups are enabled or disabled for the application segment.
Client Connector can receive CNAME: Indicates if Zscaler Client Connector receives CNAME DNS records from App Connectors.
App Connector Selection Method: Indicates if the App Connector is closest to the application or closest to users.
Inspect Traffic with ZIA: Indicates if the traffic for the application segments is enabled to be inspected with Internet & SaaS.
Active Directory Inspection: Indicates if the traffic for the application segment is inspected with Active Directory (AD) Protection protocols.
Auto App Protection: Indicates if the traffic for the application segment is inspected with AppProtection protocols.

If an application segment is missing required settings, the yellow Caution icon () appears next to its name within the table. Edit the application segment to resolve the configuration issues. If an application segment is Source IP Anchoring-enabled, the Information icon () appears next to its name within the table.

Applications: A list of up to three defined applications within the application segment. Browser Access enabled-applications are denoted by a Browser Access icon (). Privileged Remote Access (PRA)-enabled applications are denoted by a Privileged Remote Access (PRA) icon (). All other applications are denoted by a Zscaler Client Connector icon (). If there are more than three applications, then only the number of defined applications appears.
Click an application link to view its details.
For all applications, there is a link to view the Application Segment details with a list of all the applications for the application segment.
Inspection Type:
Active Directory Inspection: Indicates if the traffic for the application segment is inspected with Active Directory (AD) Protection protocols.
Auto App Protection: Indicates if the traffic for the application segment is inspected with AppProtection protocols.
Applications: Search by name, certificate, port, or protocol. Options in this section vary depending on the applications included in the application segment.
Certificate: The certificate that matches the fully qualified domain the user accesses when using Browser Access, Zero Trust Branch, or Privileged Remote Access (PRA).
Use Untrusted Certificates: Indicates whether Use Untrusted Certificates is enabled or disabled for a Browser Access-enabled or Privileged Remote Access (PRA)-enabled application.
Protocol: The protocol that the application is using.
Server Port: The web server port number used when a request is made to access a Browser Access-enabled or Privileged Remote Access (PRA)-enabled application.
Client Connector Access:
Default Port Ranges: The Port Ranges associated with the application segment.
TCP Keepalive: Indicates whether TCP Keepalive is enabled or disabled.
TCP Port Ranges: The TCP port ranges being used to access applications.
UDP Port Ranges: The UDP port ranges being used to access applications.
Tags: A list of the tags you have assigned to the application segment. To learn more, see About Tag Management.
Namespaces: The Namespaces associated with the application segment.
Key: Any keys associated with the application segment.
Values: Any values associated with the application segment.
See image.
Federated By: The partners the application is federated by (i.e., My Tenant).
Partners: The partners of the application segment.
Status: Indicates if the application segment is enabled or disabled.
Health Reporting: Indicates whether health reporting for the application is Continuous, On Access, or None.
Depending on your Zscaler Admin Console subscriptions, you can perform the following actions:
Federate an application segment and select partners to share applications with them.
View a configuration graph of connected objects.
Copy an existing application segment.
Move the application segment to a Microtenant.

The Move icon is only visible if there are one or more Microtenants available. If you are using a Microtenant, the Share icon () appears. If you share an application segment with another Microtenant, it appears as Shared to when you expand the application segment.
Enable or disable Load Balance Server Groups for an application segment.
View application segments usage details.
Edit an existing application segment.
Download the configuration information for an application segment to a CSV file.
Delete an application segment.

blocks.text: Zscaler recommends you consider the following when deleting an application segment:

blocks.item: If an application segment is referenced in a segment group and has a policy configured, the delete action is unavailable. An admin must manually review and remove the link to the policy to successfully delete the application segment. If an application segment is referenced by Internet & SaaS for Source IP Anchoring, the delete action is unavailable. A Lock icon () appears in its place. To learn more, see About Source IP Anchoring.
If an application segment is configured using Zscaler Deception, then the copy, edit, and delete options are unavailable.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
